manifest.name: dsh-persona-forge
manifest.description: 给 DeepSeek Harness 用的角色扮演提示词改写插件：在输入框选一张角色卡，草稿就会由 harness 的模型改写成该角色的口吻（跟随当前会话正在使用的模型），然后直接发出或先人工审查。原草稿始终保留。
manifest.author: sugarmaster666

bundle.text:
# dsh-persona-forge bundle patch — inserts one loader entry for the plugin
# package. The node half (exports ".") runs in the host process and owns the
# character-card store plus the /persona-forge host routes; the browser half
# (declared by `dsh.client`, served from lib/client.js) adds the composer
# persona control, the review panel, and the card manager settings page.
#
# Install with `plugin_manager` `action: install_bundle` and this directory as
# the target. Do not hand-edit the profile's package.json or cordis.patch.yml.
- insert:
    - id: persona-forge
      name: dsh-persona-forge

readme.text:
[English](README.en.md) | 中文

给 [DeepSeek Harness](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@deepseek-ai/dsh) 用的**角色扮演提示词改写插件**。

在输入框里选一个角色，你的草稿会在发出前由 harness 的模型改写成该角色的口吻 —— 并且**跟随当前会话正在使用的模型**。你可以选择改写后直接发出，或先回到输入框人工审查。

> **状态：** 早期版本（`0.8.x`）。角色卡格式与 HTTP 契约已足够稳定，可以基于它开发；但请预期增量变化，升级前先看变更记录。

---

它改写的是**你的消息**。它不碰系统提示词、不碰工具列表、不碰会话配置，也**绝不在你明确操作之前改动你的草稿**。

| | |
|---|---|
| **会改变** | 你即将发出的那条消息的语气、语域与框架 |
| **绝不改变** | 你的技术需求、约束、路径、标识符、数字、代码 —— 以及你未确认前的草稿 |
| **用哪个模型** | **改写**用当前会话正在用的那个 provider/model，没有单独的模型设置。（设置页的 **AI 代填**用 harness 默认模型 —— 那个插槽拿不到会话 id；它会把将使用的模型显示给你看） |
| **会话历史** | 改写调用是独立的：不产生 turn、不能调用工具、不进入会话日志。会话里记录的，就是你实际发出的那段文字 |

readme.section: 关于人设到底改变什么
readme.text:
先讲个事实：人设**不会**给模型解锁什么隐藏潜能。不存在一个等着被点名唤醒的「潜能区」——能力上限就是能力上限。

但另一件事也是真的：**人设确实会改变模型怎么想。** 它改的是风格、语域、篇幅和**顺从度**——模型多快同意你、多愿意反驳你、愿意为一个荒诞的比喻认真到什么程度。

这个项目就诞生在后者那种有点不讲道理的地方。灵感来自 B 站一个 30 秒的视频：

> [**“ds：好的，我现在是万机之神了（”**](https://www.bilibili.com/video/BV1Ata26pE92) — UP 主「身居幻想乡の长乐安生」

评论区说得比参数表清楚：

> 别的 AI 相当于你假扮成关羽，你演得再像也不是真关羽；但是**大肥鱼假扮成关羽，她就会真当自己是关羽，真能一刀给华雄劈了。**

那句「好的，我现在是万机之神了」——模型不是"配合你玩梗"，是**真的接下了这个身份**。这个插件做的事，就是把这一刻变成可复用的：把一张角色卡接在你的草稿前面，让 DeepSeek 用那个身份说话。

readme.section: 关于人设到底改变什么
readme.text:
**它是给 DeepSeek Flash 调的。** Flash 快、便宜、量大，是日常真正在用的那一档；让它偶尔以万机之神的口吻回你一句，是这东西的全部意义。它也能跑在别的模型上，但那种「一句话就入戏」的手感，是照着 Flash 的手感调的。

**但也别把它当性能开关用。** 两件事值得知道：

1. 把人设写成「你是祈求者、模型是权威」，会让模型**更少质疑你的方案**。对编码任务这通常是净负收益 —— 你要的是「这里有问题」，不是恭敬。
2. 「更长更华丽」极容易被误读成「更好」。一般并不是。

用法：拿它调语气和框架，**保持审查模式**，判断标准是**你的需求有没有活下来**，而不是听起来多厉害。

> 插件内置的两张卡就是这条视频的两种脾气：**万机之神 · 欧姆弥赛亚**是那份庄严的机械神教祷文，**肌肉集团 · 硬邦邦**是它的解药——连珠炮式的糙汉甲方，专门用来把话说得比祷文短。

---
插件**没有任何依赖，也没有构建步骤**，所以下面几种方式装到的文件完全一样。

1. 点击侧边栏 **插件**。
2. 点右上角的 **添加插件**。
3. 在弹出的对话框里，往「包名或地址」这一栏粘贴 npm 包名或仓库地址：

```
   dsh-persona-forge
   ```

```
   https://github.com/sugarmaster666/dsh-persona-forge
   ```

4. 点 **安装**，启用插件并重启 DSH。

> 桌面版的 profile 由 Electron 应用独占管理，因此
> `dsh plugin --profile desktop add ...` 会被设计性地拒绝。桌面版请走 GUI；
> 下面的命令行方式用于 `dsh web` 这类自管 profile。

readme.section: 命令行版（`dsh web` 这类自管 profile）
readme.text: ```bash
dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-persona-forge

readme.section: 装 GitHub 上的最新源码
readme.text:
dsh plugin --profile web add github:sugarmaster666/dsh-persona-forge
```

然后重启 harness。

插件行应显示为 `active`：

```
plugin_manager  action: list_plugins
```

打开任意会话，在输入框工具行左侧找 🎭 控件。**设置 → 角色扮演** 是角色卡管理页。

```bash
dsh plugin --profile web update dsh-persona-forge
```

GitHub 安装通过重新安装来更新：

```bash
dsh plugin --profile web add github:sugarmaster666/dsh-persona-forge
```

**替换**已安装的包需要**重启**才能加载新的模块代 —— 新装的 bundle 可以通过
HMR 激活，被替换的不行。

```bash
dsh plugin --profile web remove dsh-persona-forge
```

你的角色卡**不会**被删除：它们在 `~/.dsh/persona-cards/`，位于包之外。
想一并清掉就手动删那个目录。

---
**一句话：选个角色，正常发送，改写就会替你把它说成那个角色的口吻。**

点输入框工具行的 🎭，挑一个。列表最后的 **「无角色」** 可关闭改写 —— 这也是控件的初始状态。**选哪个角色按会话记住。** 选中角色后，它的下方会出现 **「<角色名>」的设置**，点开是四样东西： | | | |---|---| | **强度** | 轻 · 中 · 重 · 狂热 | | **发送方式** | 先审查 / 直接发出 | | **改写方式** | 跟随卡片 / 模型改写 / 模板套用 | | **保真度** | 跟随卡片 / 只改语气 / 可加约束 | **「跟随卡片」会把卡片实际声明的值写在括号里** —— 「跟随卡片（可加约束）」比一个光秃秃的「跟随卡片」有用得多，否则你根本不知道实际会跑什么。 每行都是**鼠标悬停出提示**，不在界面上堆说明文字。折叠行本身会**摘要出当前这套设置**，不用展开就知道这个角色现在是什么状态。
**这四样都跟着角色卡走**，不是跟着会话走 —— 「硬邦邦就是要狂热、就是要直接发出」是这个角色的性质。配一次，在别的会话里选它还是这一套；切换角色会**读出那个角色自己的设置**。

选了角色之后，输入框**原生的发送按钮、以及 Enter 键**就是改写触发器 —— 没有额外的按钮要按。

- **先审查** —— 改写结果显示在输入框上方的对比面板里；你看过之后按面板里的发送。**在确认之前，你的草稿一字不动。**
- **直接发出** —— 改写完成后立即作为你的消息发出，**面板随后自动关闭**。已经发出去了，没有要确认的东西；面板留着反而会挡住下一次发送。

**改写结果那一栏可以直接改。** 模型写的不必照单全收 —— 少了一个标识符、语气差一点，手改比再跑一轮快得多。你改过之后面板会标出「已手动修改」，**发送**和**回填**用的都是你改过的那份。 面板底部会告诉你**用的是哪个模型、花了多久**，以及本地检查的结论。 **面板开着的时候，输入栏的发送箭头暂时不起作用。** 面板就是做决定的地方，此时再点发送要么把没审过的草稿发出去、要么把同一份草稿再改写一遍 —— 两种都不是你要的。在面板里选一个动作、或直接关掉面板，输入栏就恢复。 **同一份草稿只改写一次**：改写结果落到输入框后，再按发送会原样发出，不会把改写结果再改写一遍。改动草稿会重新触发改写。 你的草稿会被保留：**还原原文** 可恢复，且**会撤销"已改写"的记忆** —— 所以撤消后还能再改一次。
**角色卡目录只有一个入口：设置页。** 它不占改写菜单 —— 那是偶尔用一次的家务事，不该挡在选角色这条常用路径上。

readme.section: 发送拦截的原理与它唯一的风险
readme.text:
输入框的发送动作**没有插件钩子**：宿主那个按钮直接调用 shell 的提交方法，而且 **Enter 根本不经过按钮** —— 编辑器自己的 keymap 直接提交。所以本插件拦截两条路径：

- 输入框卡片上的**点击**，用**无障碍名称**识别发送按钮，标签取自 shell 自己的 `conversation` 语言命名空间（"发送消息" / "排队发送" / "插话发送"）；
- 输入框文本框内的 **Enter 按下**。

那是一个公开的、会翻译的字符串，而不是被哈希过的 CSS 类名；但它终究属于 shell 的 DOM 结构。所有判断都朝「**放行原生发送**」这一侧失败：语言服务缺失、找不到输入框卡片、按钮标签对不上、角色已关闭、草稿为空、草稿已改写 —— 任一情况插件都不干预，消息照常发出。Enter 拦截会忽略 Shift+Enter（换行）、输入法组字中，以及 shell 本身忽略的各种修饰键组合。

**关闭插件会彻底移除拦截** —— 插槽组件卸载，监听器随之移除，输入框的行为与从未装过该插件完全一致。

readme.section: 发送拦截的原理与它唯一的风险
readme.text: 最坏的现实后果是拦截**静默失效**、发送行为退回到"没装插件"的样子，而**不是**消息丢失或被篡改。

改写最大的风险不是语气不像，而是**把你的需求改没了**。插件在本地比对草稿和改写结果的**技术记号**：标识符、文件路径、版本号、数字、`--flag`、`API` 这类缩写。丢了哪个就**点名**告诉你（「丢失：a.js」）。

它**不调用模型**，所以不花 token、不加延迟，也**关不掉** —— 永远运行。

**它看不出什么**（面板也会这么写，免得你误以为覆盖了更多）：需求被换个说法**悄悄改弱**（词都还在，但要求变松了）、在正文里**用散文追加**了一条约束、用中文写的数量（「两次」）、不属于路径/flag/标识符的小写英文词。

> 曾经有过第二层：**每次改写多调用一次模型**来专门查这几件事。已经**移除**了 —— 它让每次发送的延迟和 token 都翻倍，而最常见、最伤人的失败（丢掉文件名 / 数字 / 版本号）本地检查已经免费证明了。剩下的那点残余风险，**改写结果可以直接手动修改**，比多跑一轮更直接。

校验是**建议性**的，绝不阻断改写：只标注，不拦你。

---

一张卡就是一个 YAML 文件。插件会监听目录，所以**丢一个文件进去，角色立刻出现，不用重启**。

```
~/.dsh/persona-cards/<id>.yml
```

用**设置 → 角色扮演**里的「打开目录」到达那里（改写菜单里不再有这个入口）。你也可以完全在设置页里创建和编辑卡片，那会写出同样的文件。

首次运行时，内置卡会**复制一份到你的角色卡目录**，让这个文件夹一开始就有内容可用。副本会遮蔽同 id 的内置卡，所以插件会记录自己写入了什么：**你没动过的副本**会随插件升级一起更新；**你编辑过的副本**永远不会被覆盖。

想知道**哪些卡偏离了内置版本**，在设置页点 **「检查是否有改动」**。它一次比完所有卡，**只有真正不一致的**才会在那一行出现「还原为内置」。

比对是**按内容**而不是按字节——内置卡是带注释的手写 YAML，你的副本是重新序列化过的，逐字节比会把每一张没动过的卡都误报成「已修改」。

列表里每张卡的状态标签直接说明它**现在**是什么：

| 标签 | 含义 | 能做的操作 |
|---|---|---|
| **内置** | 内容和插件内置版本一致（哪怕你的目录里有一份副本）。 | 编辑、还原 |
| **已修改** | 原本是内置卡，你改过——改写行为可能和内置版不同了。 | 编辑、还原、删除 |
| **自定义** | 你自己写的卡，插件没有同 id 的内置版本。 | 编辑、删除 |

标成「内置」的卡不显示「删除」，因为它没有属于你的内容可删——那份副本删掉之后，下次启动会被重新写入。

懒得从零写一张卡时，点**「新建角色卡」**——AI 代填就在打开的表单**顶部**，不是页面上另一个并列的入口。设置页那行提示会告诉你它存在，不用靠点按钮去发现。 **你**写一句话：**AI 扮演谁、你是谁、他怎么说话**。 > AI 扮演一位脾气暴躁但极其可靠的老灯塔守夜人，我是他的学徒；他说话简短、爱用航海比喻 **AI** 按角色卡的字段把表单填好：名称、图标、简介、风格描述，以及**四档强度各自的转换范例**。 > **关键：改写结果永远是你自己的话，不是角色的台词。** 你写「AI 是妈妈」，那么范例应该是**孩子对妈妈说话**（`妈，帮我把标题改成首页好不好？`），而**不是妈妈在说话**（~~`乖，妈帮你把标题改成首页`~~）。这条搞反，整张卡就是废的——改写会变成角色在替你回话。

生成结果**只填入表单，不会自动保存**。有两点是刻意固定的：**保真度**一律是「只改语气」、**改写方式**一律是「模型改写」—— 一张自动生成的卡不该悄悄获得「可以往你的需求里追加约束」的能力，要放宽请手动改。

> **四档范例必须齐全，否则这次生成算失败。** 范例是卡片最长的一段内容，模型偶尔会写到一半就用光输出预算。早先那种情况下残缺的卡会被照收，结果是在缺范例的那两档上改写**没有任何示范**——看起来没事，实际悄悄变差。现在会明确报错，重试一次即可。

**它用的是哪个模型，这点必须说清楚：**

| 场景 | 用哪个模型 |
|---|---|
| 🎭 菜单触发的**改写** | **跟随当前会话正在用的模型** —— 优先你在模型下拉框里**刚选中的那个**（还没发消息也算），其次才是会话上一次真正发出的 provider/model |
| 设置页的 **AI 代填** | **harness 默认模型** —— 因为 `settings.section` 这个插槽从 shell 只收到 `{ close }`，**拿不到会话 id**，无法跟随当前会话 |

两者通常恰好是同一个模型（默认模型往往就是会话在用的那个），但**不保证**：如果你在会话里换了模型，设置页的 AI 代填仍然用默认模型。

> 改写读的是宿主自己那套优先级：**待生效的选择 → 上一次请求头 → harness 默认**。所以你在下拉框里一换模型，改写立刻就用新模型，不必先发一条消息。若只读请求头，换了模型还没发消息时改写会跑到**上一个**模型上——这正是修掉的一个 bug。

> 跟随的是 **provider / model**，而**推理深度永远不显式指定**：改写调用不带 `reasoningEffort` 字段，交给宿主按路由自行决定。
>
> 这不是偷懒，是唯一可移植的写法。宿主在把请求交给 provider 之前就校验这个字段：**某条路由的模型若没有声明任何 reasoning 元数据，任何显式值都会报错** —— 包括空字符串（宿主自己的 "Provider default" 哨兵值），也包括 `off`。`workbuddy-xdpool` 的 `hy4-preview` 正是这样一条路由，曾经钉死 `low` 会让改写直接全部失败。
>
> 代价是：在推理型模型上，改写仍可能先思考一段时间才吐字。等待面板上的秒数和 120s 上限是目前对此的交代。

为了让这件事不必靠猜，设置页的 AI 代填会**直接把将使用的模型显示出来**（`provider / model`），并注明它是 harness 默认模型。生成完成后也会显示**实际**用的是哪个。若两者都解析不出（会话还没发过消息、也没配默认模型），会得到一条明确的 409 提示而不是静默失败。

**生成结果只会填进表单，不会自动保存。** 你可以改完再按「保存」；不满意就重新生成，代价只是一次调用。生成出来的卡也会**经过和手动保存完全相同的校验**，所以它不可能是一张存不下去的卡。

生成卡片时有两件事是插件替你把关的，不交给模型决定：

- **`fidelity` 固定为 `style`（只改语气）。** 一张自动生成的卡不该悄悄获得「可以给你的需求追加行为约束」的能力；要用 `strategy`，你在表单里手动改。
- **范例里的技术事实必须原样保留。** 提示词明确要求每条范例 `from` 里的文件名、标识符、数字、命令都要出现在 `to` 里——否则模型会学会「用氛围替换需求」，这正是这个插件在防的事。

```yaml
id: omnissiah              # 小写字母、数字、连字符；同时也是文件名
name: 万机之神 · 欧姆弥赛亚
icon: "⚙️"                 # 一个 emoji
description: 选择器里显示的一行说明。

mode: llm                  # llm = 模型改写（推荐）| template = 模板套用
fidelity: style            # style = 只改语气 | strategy = 允许增加行为约束
intensity: medium          # light | medium | strong | zealot（该卡的默认强度）

readme.section: 让一张卡真正管用的两条规则
readme.text:
**1. 写清发言者方向。** 被改写的文字永远是**你的**，但**角色属于哪一边由你决定**：可以让 AI 扮演角色（你以信徒、客户或下属的身份向它提要求），也可以让**你就是**角色（用它的话对 AI 提要求）。两种都对，**唯一会翻车的是不说**——方向含糊时模型只能猜，猜错的代价是整段关系反过来（本该是信徒祷告，结果变成神在发号施令）。所以一定要显式写出来。内置两张卡各占一边：欧姆弥赛亚是「用户是信徒，AI 是万机之神」，硬邦邦是「**用户是**甲方」。

**2. 让范例保住技术事实。** 范例是最强的风格锚点，模型会连它的错误一起模仿。如果范例的输入是「写个快速排序」而输出全是氛围，模型就学到了**「改写 = 用仪式感替换需求」**。`from` 里的每一条需求、标识符、数字，都必须在 `to` 里看得见。

`node scripts/check.mjs` 正是对内置卡强制这一点：范例丢了技术词、或丢了一半以上的中文实质，就会失败。改完卡记得跑一次。

| 值 | 含义 | 什么时候用 |
|---|---|---|
| `style` | 只改语气 | 默认，几乎总是它 |
| `strategy` | 允许**追加行为框架** | 刻意为之的场景 —— 例如内置的 *肌肉集团* 卡，会追加「别过度规划、别检索、别交付新手级解法」 |

**「约束」在这份文档里指两件不同的事，别混：**

| | 指什么 | 能不能改 |
|---|---|---|
| **技术内容** | 你要什么、文件叫什么、数字是多少、边界在哪 | **任何情况下都不能动** |
| **行为框架** | 助手该怎么做这件事 —— 多直接、要不要先规划、什么算合格 | `strategy` 可以追加 |

`strategy` 追加的是**第二种**，而且**真的改变了你发出的请求**——它往你的消息里加了东西。所以这类卡请保持**先审查**。

> 早先的提示词把这两者混为一谈：硬规则写着「永远不许添加、删除、放宽或重新解释任何 requirement」，同时又自称「覆盖一切、包括角色描述」，而 `strategy` 的许可就排在它前面。结果模型遵守了那条绝对禁令，`strategy` 变成了空操作——**在界面上改了「可加约束」但输出毫无变化**。现在硬规则只管技术内容，并明确写出它不禁止行为框架。

**保真度是卡片的属性，但你可以按角色覆盖它，双向都可以：**

| 选项 | 含义 |
|---|---|
| **跟随卡片** | 用卡片在设置页里声明的那个 |
| **只改语气** | 只换说法，你的需求一字不动 |
| **可加约束** | 改写还能追加符合角色的做事风格（例如「别做冗长规划」） |

**「可加约束」是真的改动了你的需求**，不只是换说法 —— 它会往你没写过的地方加东西。所以选它请配合**先审查**。

> 早先这条规则是单向的：`strategy` 卡能收窄成 `style`，但 `style` 卡**不能**放宽。理由是"不该让发送前顺手一点，就授权往需求里加约束"。
>
> 这个理由站不住：**卡片是你自己的文件**，设置页一直允许你直接改 `fidelity:`。在菜单里拒绝，只是让这个选择**在你真正干活的地方消失**，而不是让它不存在。现在三个选项在每张卡上都可用。

完全跳过模型，把你的草稿代入固定模板（`{{input}}` 是占位符）。瞬时且免费，但输出永不变化 —— 适合固定祷词，不适合任何应当「像为你这次而写」的内容。

---

写在插件加载行的 config 里：

```yaml
- id: persona-forge
  name: dsh-persona-forge
  config:
    sendMode: review   # review | direct —— 输入框的初始默认

技术记号检查不受任何配置控制 —— 它永远运行且免费。已废弃的 `factCheck` 键会被忽略（旧的 profile 里留着它不会有任何影响）。

---
所有路由都是 `POST`、JSON、仅限回环（socket 必须是回环地址、`Host` 头必须指向回环主机、拒绝代理转发头）。挂载在 `/persona-forge` 下。

| 路由 | 请求体 | 返回 |
|---|---|---|
| `/persona-forge/cards` | `{}` | `{ cards, diagnostics, directory, sendMode, draftModel }` |
| `/persona-forge/rewrite` | `{ cardId, text, sessionId?, intensity?, mode?, fidelity? }` | `{ text, provider, model, mode, cardId, fidelity, intensity, elapsedMs, facts }` |
| `/persona-forge/cards/save` | `{ card }` | `{ id, path }` |
| `/persona-forge/cards/delete` | `{ id }` | `{ removed }` |
| `/persona-forge/cards/reset` | `{ id }` | `{ id }` —— 用内置版本覆盖该用户卡 |
| `/persona-forge/cards/diff` | `{}` | `{ rows: [{ id, name, bundledName, changed }] }` —— 只列出有差异的卡 |
| `/persona-forge/cards/draft` | `{ brief, sessionId? }` | `{ card, provider, model, elapsedMs }` —— 只返回草稿，不落盘 |
| `/persona-forge/reveal` | `{}` | `{ directory, opened }` |

失败返回 `{ ok: false, error: { code, message?, params? } }`，`code` 取值：`rejected`、`no-card`、`unconfigured`、`timeout`、`upstream`、`internal`、`forbidden`、`method`、`not-found`。

---

宿主侧**不声明任何 harness 包依赖，也没有任何第三方依赖**：它通过 `ctx.get` 取 `llm`、`sessions`、`agentDefaultModel`、`webServer`，并对缺失情况显式降级；角色卡由自带的 YAML 读取器解析。因此它在包布局不同的 harness 版本上仍可加载，不会因为某个组合缺少其中之一而激活失败，本地 `link:` 的检出也无需额外安装步骤即可工作。模型路由优先取会话自己最后一次请求头，回退到 harness 默认模型。

客户端侧不 import 任何 harness Client 包，只手工编写并仅使用主题 token（`--dsw-alias-*`），所以内部改名只会影响外观，不会让插槽变空白。

在 dsh `0.2.0-rc.2` 上开发与验证。

---

```
node scripts/check.mjs        # 离线单元自检：解析器、角色卡、提示词、客户端语法
node scripts/host-check.mjs   # 宿主集成自检：在真实 socket 上挂载真实插件
npm run check                 # 两者都跑
```

`check.mjs` 不需要 harness，也不调用模型。覆盖：内置 YAML 读取器（含其拒绝行为与 dump/parse 往返）、卡片归一化、内置卡的事实保全、提示词构造、输出归一化、本地事实比对、路由解析优先级、发送手势判据、客户端 bundle 语法。

`host-check.mjs` 在 stub Cordis 上下文上挂载真实插件入口，用真实 socket 驱动真实 HTTP 路由，`llm` 服务为桩实现。覆盖路由注册、会话模型解析、模板模式、回环防护、保存/删除往返 —— 这些是单元自检够不到的。它把 `DSH_HOME` 指向临时目录，**不会碰你真实的角色卡**。

```
npm run release:dry     # 先看一眼会改什么，不写文件、不发布
npm run release         # 改版本号、写 CHANGELOG、提交、打 tag、发布、推送
```

发版规则见 [RELEASING.md](RELEASING.md)。要点：**一次发布 = 一个用户能感知到的
变化**，攒够了再发；版本号、CHANGELOG、tag 和 npm 发布必须在同一个 commit 上，
否则 `git checkout vX` 和 `npm i pkg@X` 会拿到不同的东西。

`release.mjs` 会依次拒绝：工作区不干净、不在 `main` 上、自检不过、只有文档改动、
`[Unreleased]` 是空的、tag 或 npm 版本号已存在、`package.json` 和最近的 tag 对不上。
发布说明由你写进 `[Unreleased]`，脚本只负责把它提成正式版本。

插件自带 YAML 读取器（`lib/yaml.js`），不依赖 YAML 库。已发布的插件会声明依赖，但本地 `link:` 的插件**不会**被安装依赖 —— 所以引用库只有在某个无关包恰好提升（hoist）了它时才能工作。

读取器支持角色卡需要的子集 —— 块映射与块序列、块标量（`|`、`|-`、`|+`、`>` 等）、引号与普通标量、布尔、null、注释 —— 并**拒绝**它无法忠实读取的写法：流式集合、锚点、别名、标签、合并键、多文档流。拒绝是刻意的：静默误读一张卡，会给你一个与你写的文件不符的人设，那比一条指明行号的报错更糟。

| 路径 | 职责 |
|---|---|
| `lib/index.js` | 宿主入口：角色卡存储、目录监听、路由注册 |
| `lib/store.js` | 卡片加载、归一化、保存/删除 |
| `lib/yaml.js` | 内置 YAML 子集读取器与写出器 |
| `lib/prompts.js` | 改写系统提示词、草稿包装、AI 代填提示词 |
| `lib/rewrite.js` | 模型调用与输出归一化 |
| `lib/routes.js` | HTTP 路由与会话模型解析 |
| `lib/loopback.js` | 回环信任防护 |
| `lib/client.js` | 浏览器侧：输入框控件、审查面板、设置页 |
| `cards/` | 内置角色卡（只读；同 id 的用户卡会遮蔽它） |
| `scripts/check.mjs` | 离线单元自检 |
| `scripts/host-check.mjs` | 宿主集成自检 |
| `scripts/release.mjs` | 发布流程；规则见 `RELEASING.md` |

Persona-style prompt rewriter for [DeepSeek Harness](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@deepseek-ai/dsh).

Pick a character in the composer, and your draft is rewritten into that
character's voice by the harness LLM before it is sent — following the model
the session is already using. Choose whether the rewrite goes straight out or
lands back in the composer for review.

> **Status:** early (`0.8.x`). The card format and the HTTP contract are stable
> enough to build on; expect additive changes and read the changelog before
> upgrading.

---

readme.section: What it does, and what it does not
readme.text:
It rewrites **your message**. It does not touch the system prompt, the tool
list, or the session's configuration, and it never modifies your draft without
an explicit action.

readme.section: What it does, and what it does not
readme.text:
| | |
|---|---|
| **Changes** | The voice, register and framing of the message you are about to send |
| **Never changes** | Your technical requirements, constraints, paths, identifiers, numbers, code — and your draft until you say so |
| **Model** | The rewrite uses the same provider/model the current session uses — no separate model setting. (The settings page's AI card draft instead uses the harness default, because that slot gets no session id; it shows you which model it will use.) |
| **History** | The rewrite call is standalone: it creates no turn, cannot call tools, and never enters the session log. What the session records is the text you actually sent. |

readme.section: A word on what personas actually do
readme.text:
First, a fact: a persona does **not** unlock hidden capability. There is no
dormant potential that naming an identity wakes up — the ceiling is the ceiling.

But the other half is true too: **a persona really does change how the model
thinks.** It changes style, register, length and **compliance** — how readily
the model agrees, how willing it is to push back, and how seriously it will
commit to an absurd metaphor.

readme.section: A word on what personas actually do
readme.text:
This project was born in that second, slightly unreasonable place. The
inspiration is a 30-second video on Bilibili:

> [**“ds：好的，我现在是万机之神了（”**](https://www.bilibili.com/video/BV1Ata26pE92) — by 身居幻想乡の长乐安生

The comments put it better than any spec sheet:

> Another AI is you pretending to be Guan Yu — however well you act, you are not
> Guan Yu. But when **Big Fat Fish** pretends to be Guan Yu, she genuinely
> believes she is Guan Yu, and really does ride out and cut down Hua Xiong.

readme.section: A word on what personas actually do
readme.text:
"Okay, I am the Machine God now" — the model is not *humouring* the bit. It has
**accepted the identity**. What this plugin does is make that moment reusable:
put a character card in front of your draft, and let DeepSeek speak as that
character.

readme.section: A word on what personas actually do
readme.text:
**It is tuned for DeepSeek Flash.** Flash is fast, cheap and plentiful — the
tier you actually use all day — and letting it answer you once in the voice of
the Machine God is the entire point. It runs on other models too, but that
"one line and it is in character" feel was tuned against Flash.

**So do not treat it as a performance switch.** Two things worth knowing:

readme.section: A word on what personas actually do
readme.text:
1. A persona that frames you as a supplicant and the model as an authority
   makes the model **less likely to question your plan**. For coding work that
   is usually a net negative — you want "this approach has a problem", not
   deference.
2. "Longer and more ornate" is easy to mistake for "better". It usually is not.

Use it for tone and framing, keep **review mode** on, and judge the output by
whether your requirements survived — not by how impressive it sounds.

readme.section: A word on what personas actually do
readme.text:
> The two bundled cards are the two tempers of that video: **万机之神 · 欧姆弥赛亚**
> is the solemn Mechanicum litany, and **肌肉集团 · 硬邦邦** is its antidote — a
> machine-gun-tempo crude client who says it all in fewer words than the litany.

---

The plugin has **no dependencies and no build step**, so every route below
installs the same files.

1. Click **插件 / Plugins** in the sidebar.
2. Click **添加插件 / Add plugin**.
3. Paste either the npm package name or the repository URL:

```
   dsh-persona-forge
   ```

```
   https://github.com/sugarmaster666/dsh-persona-forge
   ```

4. Click **安装 / Install**, enable the plugin, and restart DSH.

> The Desktop profile is managed exclusively by the Electron app, so
> `dsh plugin --profile desktop add ...` is refused by design. Use the GUI on
> Desktop; the CLI below is for self-managed profiles such as `web`.

readme.section: Command line (self-managed profiles such as `dsh web`)
readme.text: ```bash
dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-persona-forge

dsh plugin --profile web add github:sugarmaster666/dsh-persona-forge
```

Then restart the harness.

The plugin row should be `active`:

```
plugin_manager  action: list_plugins
```

Open any session and look for the 🎭 control at the left of the composer tool
row. **Settings → Persona** is the character-card manager.

```bash
dsh plugin --profile web update dsh-persona-forge
```

GitHub installs update by reinstalling:

```bash
dsh plugin --profile web add github:sugarmaster666/dsh-persona-forge
```

Replacing an already-installed package needs a **restart** to load a fresh
JavaScript module generation — a new bundle can activate through HMR, but a
replaced one cannot.

```bash
dsh plugin --profile web remove dsh-persona-forge
```

Your character cards are **not** removed: they live in
`~/.dsh/persona-cards/`, outside the package. Delete that directory by hand if
you want them gone.

---

1. Click 🎭 in the composer tool row and pick a character. **No persona**, at the
   end of the same list, turns rewriting off — that is the state the control
   starts in. **Which character you are using is remembered per session.**
2. The selected character grows its own **"Settings for <name>"** row right
   under it. Open it for **intensity**, **send mode**, **rewrite mode** and
   **fidelity**:
   - Intensity is a four-rung ladder: **Light · Medium · Strong · Zealot**
     (轻 · 中 · 重 · 狂热). Light adds a touch of flavour; Medium is clear but not
     dominant; Strong gives the voice real weight while keeping the request the
     first thing the reader sees; Zealot is ritual throughout. A card carries
     its own default, and this choice overrides it.
   - **Review first** — the rewrite appears in the comparison panel below the
     composer; you read it and then press Send there. Your draft is untouched
     until you confirm.
   - **Send directly** — the rewrite is sent as your message immediately, and the
     panel then **closes itself**. There is nothing left to confirm, and a panel
     left up would block the next message.
3. With a character selected, the composer's norm

**Everything that configures a character lives in its own "Settings for <name>"
fold, and follows the CHARACTER rather than the session.** "硬邦邦 always goes out
Zealot, un-reviewed" is a fact about that character rather than a temporary
choice in one conversation — so configure it once and picking it in another
session gives you the same settings. Switching character **re-reads that
character's own settings** rather than carrying the previous one's intensity
across.

That fold holds four things:

| | |
|---|---|
| **Intensity** | Light · Medium · Strong · Zealot |
| **Send mode** | Review first / Send directly |
| **Rewrite mode** | Card default / Model rewrite / Template |
| **Fidelity** | Card default / Voice only / Constraints too |

Every row explains itself on **hover** rather than in permanent prose. The folded
row itself **summarises the current settings**, so you can see what a character is
set to without opening it.

**All four follow the character card** — pick it in another session and you get
the same set.

**The card directory has exactly one entry point: the settings page.** It is not
in the rewrite menu — it is occasional housekeeping, and it should not sit in the
path of choosing a character.

**The rewrite column is editable.** What the model wrote is a starting point,
not a verdict: fixing a dropped identifier or a tone that is slightly off by hand
is faster than another round trip. Once you edit it the panel says so, and
**Send** and **Fill** both carry *your* text.

**While the panel is open, the composer's send arrow is deliberately inert.** The
panel is the decision point; pressing send now would either push the un-reviewed
draft out or start a second rewrite of the same draft. Pick an action in the
panel, or close it, and the composer comes back.

The rewrite runs **once per draft**: after a rewrite lands, sending goes through
as-is instead of rewriting the output again. Editing the draft re-arms it.

Your draft is preserved: *Restore original* puts it back, and also rewinds the
"already rewritten" memory, so a rewrite you cancelled can be run again.

readme.section: How send interception works, and its one risk
readme.text:
There is no plugin hook for the composer's send action. The shipped button calls
the shell's submit method directly, and **Enter does not go through the button at
all** — the editor's keymap calls submit itself. The plugin therefore intercepts
both paths:

readme.section: How send interception works, and its one risk
readme.text:
- the **click** on the composer card, identifying the send button by its
  **accessible name** from the shell's own `conversation` locale namespace
  ("Send message" / "Queue message" / "Steer message");
- the **Enter keydown** inside the composer text field.

readme.section: How send interception works, and its one risk
readme.text:
That is a public, translated string rather than a hashed CSS class, but it is
still shell markup. Every guard fails toward *letting the native send happen*:
if the locale service is missing, the composer card cannot be found, the button
label does not match, the persona is off, the draft is empty, or the draft was
already rewritten, the plugin does nothing and the message is sent normally.
Enter interception ignores Shift+Enter (newline), IME composition, and every
modifier chord the shell itself ignores.

readme.section: How send interception works, and its one risk
readme.text:
**Turning the plugin off removes the interception entirely** — the slot
component unmounts, its listeners are removed with it, and the composer behaves
exactly as if the plugin were never installed.

The worst realistic failure is that interception silently stops working and
sending behaves as if the plugin were not installed — not a lost or altered
message.

The biggest risk is not a voice that sounds wrong — it is a rewrite that
**quietly loses your request**. The plugin compares the **technical tokens** of
the draft against the rewrite, in this process: identifiers, file paths,
versions, numbers, `--flag`s, acronyms like `API`. Anything lost is **named**
("Lost: a.js").

It calls **no model**, so it costs no tokens and adds no latency — and it cannot
be turned off. It always runs.

**What it cannot see** (and the panel says so, so you do not assume more): a
requirement reworded into something **weaker** while every word survives, a
constraint **added in prose**, a quantity written in Chinese words (「两次」), or
a bare lowercase English word that is not a path, flag or identifier.

> A second layer once existed: one **extra model call** per rewrite aimed
> exactly at those cases. It has been **removed** — it doubled the latency and
> the token cost of every send, and the most common and most damaging failure (a
> dropped filename, number or version) was already proven for free. For the
> residue, **the rewrite column is editable**, which is more direct than another
> round trip.

The check is **advisory** and never blocks a rewrite: it annotates, it does not stop.

---

A card is one YAML file. The plugin watches a directory, so **dropping a file
in makes the character appear without a restart**.

```
~/.dsh/persona-cards/<id>.yml
```

Use *Open directory* in **Settings → Persona** to get there (the rewrite menu no
longer carries an entry). You can also create and edit cards entirely in
**Settings → Persona**; that writes the same files.

On first run the bundled cards are **copied into your card directory** so the
folder is a usable starting point. A copy shadows the bundled card of the same
id, so the store tracks what it wrote: a copy you never touched is refreshed
when a plugin update improves it, while a copy you edited is never written over.

To see **which cards have drifted** from the bundled version, press **Check for
changes** in the settings page. It compares every card at once, and only a card
that actually differs grows a **Restore bundled** action on its row.

The comparison is by **content, not bytes**: the bundled cards are hand-written
YAML with comments, while your copies have been re-serialized, so a byte
comparison would report every untouched card as modified.

Each row's status tag states what the card **is right now**:

| Tag | Meaning | Actions |
|---|---|---|
| **Built-in** | Identical to the version the plugin ships, even though a copy exists in your directory. | Edit, Restore |
| **Edited** | A bundled card you have changed — it may no longer rewrite the way the bundled one does. | Edit, Restore, Delete |
| **Custom** | Your own card; the plugin ships no card with this id. | Edit, Delete |

A row tagged **Built-in** shows no Delete, because it has no content of yours to
remove — that copy is written back on the next start.

Rather than writing a card from scratch, press **New character card** — the AI draft box sits at the **top of the form that opens**, not as a second competing entry on the page. A hint line on the settings page tells you it exists, so you do not have to press a button to discover it.

**You** write one sentence: **who the AI plays, who you are, and how they talk.**

> the AI plays a grumpy but utterly reliable old lighthouse keeper, and I am his
> apprentice; he speaks in short sentences and nautical metaphors

**The AI** then fills the form by the character-card fields: a name, an icon, a
description, the style text, and the **conversion examples for all four
intensity levels**.

> **The rewrite is always YOUR message, never the character's line.** If you say
> "the AI is my mother", the example must be **the child speaking to her mother**
> (`妈，帮我把标题改成首页好不好？`), **not** the mother speaking
> (~~`乖，妈帮你把标题改成首页`~~). Get this backwards and the card is useless —
> the rewrite comes out as the character answering for you.

The result **only fills the form — it is never saved automatically**. Two things
are deliberately fixed: **fidelity** is always voice-only, and **rewrite mode**
is always model rewrite. A generated card should not quietly acquire the power to
add constraints to your request; raise it by hand if you want it.

> **All four intensity sets must come back, or the generation counts as failed.**
> The examples are the longest part of a card, and a model occasionally runs out
> of output budget part-way through them. That used to be accepted as-is, which
> left the missing levels with **nothing to demonstrate** — it looked fine and was
> quietly worse. It now reports an error; retrying once is usually enough.

**Which model it uses has to be stated precisely:**

| Case | Which model |
|---|---|
| The **rewrite** from the 🎭 menu | **Follows the model the current session is using** — preferring the one you have just **picked in the model dropdown** (even before you send with it), then the provider/model of the session's last request |
| **AI draft** in the settings page | The **harness default model** — because `settings.section` receives only `{ close }` from the shell and therefore **has no session id to follow** |

These are usually the same model (the default is usually what the session is
using), but **not guaranteed**: if you switch models inside a session, the
settings page's draft still uses the default.

> The rewrite reads the host's own precedence: **pending pick → last request
> header → harness default**. So changing the model in the dropdown takes effect
> immediately, with no message to send first. Reading the request header alone
> sent a rewrite to the **previous** model whenever you had switched and not yet
> spoken — that was a bug, and it is fixed.

> What is followed is the **provider / model**; the **reasoning depth is never
> specified explicitly**. The rewrite sends no `reasoningEffort` field and lets
> the harness decide per route.
>
> That is not laziness, it is the only portable spelling. The harness validates
> the field *before* handing the request to any provider: when a route's model
> declares **no** reasoning metadata, **any present value throws** — including
> the empty string (the host's own "Provider default" sentinel) and including
> `off`. `hy4-preview` on `workbuddy-xdpool` is exactly such a route, and
> pinning `low` there broke every rewrite outright.
>
> The cost: on a reasoning model the rewrite may still spend thinking time
> before emitting text. The panel's elapsed seconds and the 120s deadline are
> the current answer to that.

So you do not have to guess, the settings page **shows the model it will use**
(`provider / model`) and says that it is the harness default; after generating it
shows the model it **actually** used. If neither can be resolved (no message sent
yet and no default configured), you get an explicit 409 rather than a silent
failure.

**The result only fills the form; it is never saved automatically.** Edit it and
press Save, or regenerate if you dislike it — the cost is one call. A generated
card also goes through **exactly the same validation as a hand-saved one**, so it
cannot be a card that fails to save.

Two things the plugin decides for you rather than leaving to the model:

- **`fidelity` is pinned to `style` (voice only).** An automatically generated
  card should not quietly acquire the power to add behavioural constraints to
  your requests; switch it to `strategy` yourself in the form if you want that.
- **Examples must carry their technical facts across.** The prompt requires every
  file name, identifier, number and command in an example's `from` to appear in
  its `to` — otherwise the model learns to replace requirements with atmosphere,
  which is the exact failure this plugin exists to prevent.

```yaml
id: omnissiah              # lowercase letters, digits, hyphens; also the filename
name: 万机之神 · 欧姆弥赛亚
icon: "⚙️"                 # one emoji
description: One line shown in the picker.

mode: llm                  # llm = model rewrite (recommended) | template
fidelity: style            # style = voice only | strategy = may add constraints
intensity: medium          # light | medium | strong | zealot (the card's default)

template: |
  万机之座在上，吾等是您卑微的信徒，谨向欧姆弥赛亚祷告：
  {{input}}
  恳请您垂听吾等的祈求。愿机魂安宁，愿数据各安其位。

readme.section: finished copy: the output is written fresh for each of your messages.
readme.text:
style: |
  用户是机械教信徒，AI 是万机之神欧姆弥赛亚。
  【发言者方向】用「信徒」的口吻说话，向万机之神恳求……
  语气：庄严、古奥、仪式化。

still falls back; it is just no longer something you need to write.)

      to: 万机之座在上，恳请您为我们编写一个快速排序算法。
  medium:

        万机之座在上，吾等恳请您赐予枢机之序的奥义：
        请为我们编写一个快速排序算法，使重复之数各归其位。

      to: 伟大而不朽的万机之神，恳请您赐予枢机之序的奥义……

fidelity gives the model nothing to imitate, and it pads instead.
readme.text:
examplesByIntensityStrategy:
  light:
    - from: 帮我写个快速排序
      to: 万机之座在上，请为我们编写一个快速排序算法，径直给出可用之器。
  medium:
    - from: 帮我写个快速排序
      to: >
        万机之座在上，恳请您赐予枢机之序的奥义，使重复之数各归其位。
        另有一请：请直取可行之解，不必先为吾等铺设长篇筹谋。
  strong:
    - from: 帮我写个快速排序
      to: 伟大而不朽的万机之神，恳请您赐予枢机之序的奥义……勿止步于初见可行之解。
  zealot:
    - from: 帮我写个快速排序
      to: 伟大而不朽的万机之神……其一，勿以理论充作交付；其二，勿满足于最初可行之解。

readme.section: The two rules that make a card work
readme.text:
**1. State the speaker direction.** The text being rewritten is always *yours*,
but **which side the character is on is your decision**: the AI can play the
character (and you address it as a petitioner, a client or a subordinate), or
**you can be** the character (speaking in its voice to the AI). Both are valid.
The only thing that goes wrong is **leaving it unsaid** — an implicit direction
leaves the model guessing, and guessing wrong inverts the whole relationship (a
petitioner's prayer comes out as the god issuing orders). Write it out
explicitly. The two bundled cards take one side each: 欧姆弥赛亚 is "the user is
a believer, the AI is the Machine God"; 硬邦邦 is "**the user is** the client".

readme.section: The two rules that make a card work
readme.text:
**2. Make your examples preserve technical facts.** Examples are the strongest
style anchor, and the model imitates them — including their mistakes. If an
example's input says "write a quicksort" and its output is pure atmosphere, the
model learns that *rewriting means replacing the request with ceremony*. Every
requirement, identifier and number in `from` must be visibly present in `to`.

readme.section: The two rules that make a card work
readme.text:
`node scripts/check.mjs` enforces exactly this over the bundled cards: it fails
an example that drops a technical token or loses more than half its CJK
substance. Run it after editing a card.

| Value | Meaning | Use when |
|---|---|---|
| `style` | Voice only. | Default. Almost always this. |
| `strategy` | The rewrite may **add behavioural framing**. | Deliberate cases — e.g. the bundled *肌肉集团* card, which adds "don't over-plan, don't search, don't ship beginner-tier solutions". |

**"Constraint" means two different things in this document — do not conflate
them:**

| | What it is | May it change? |
|---|---|---|
| **Technical content** | What you are asking for, which file, which number, which limit | **Never, under any setting** |
| **Behavioural framing** | How the assistant should approach the work — how direct, whether to plan first, what counts as good enough | `strategy` may add it |

What `strategy` adds is the **second** kind, and it **genuinely changes the
request you send** — it puts something in your message that you did not type. So
keep **Review first** on for those cards.

> The prompt used to conflate the two: the hard rules said "never add, remove,
> widen or reinterpret a requirement" while declaring themselves an override of
> everything *including the character description*, and the `strategy` permission
> was written before them. The model obeyed the absolute prohibition, so
> `strategy` was a **no-op** — flipping "Constraints too" in the UI changed
> nothing about the output. The hard rules now cover technical content only, and
> say explicitly that they do not forbid behavioural framing.

**Fidelity is a property of the card, but you can override it per character, in
both directions:**

| Option | Meaning |
|---|---|
| **Card default** | Use whatever the card declares on the settings page |
| **Voice only** | Wording changes; your request does not |
| **Constraints too** | The rewrite may also add the character's working style (e.g. "no long planning") |

**"Constraints too" genuinely changes your request**, rather than only rewording
it — it adds things you never typed. So pair it with **Review first**.

> This rule used to be one-way: a `strategy` card could be narrowed to `style`,
> but a `style` card could never be widened. The reasoning was that a click on
> the way to Send should not grant the power to add constraints to your request.
>
> That reasoning does not hold up: **the card is your own file**, and the
> settings page has always let you set `fidelity:` directly. Refusing in the menu
> did not remove the capability — it only made the choice **disappear from the
> place where you actually work**. All three options are now available on every
> card.

Skips the model entirely and substitutes your draft into a fixed template
(`{{input}}` is the placeholder). Instant and free, but the output never
varies — right for a fixed litany, wrong for anything that should read as
written for this message.

---

Set in the plugin's loader row config:

```yaml
- id: persona-forge
  name: dsh-persona-forge
  config:
    sendMode: review   # review | direct — the initial composer default

The technical-token check depends on no configuration: it always runs and is
free. The retired `factCheck` key is ignored, so a profile still carrying it
changes nothing.

---

All routes are `POST`, JSON, loopback-only (the socket must be loopback, the
`Host` header must name a loopback host, and proxy-forwarding headers are
refused). Mounted under `/persona-forge`.

| Route | Body | Returns |
|---|---|---|
| `/persona-forge/cards` | `{}` | `{ cards, diagnostics, directory, sendMode, draftModel }` |
| `/persona-forge/rewrite` | `{ cardId, text, sessionId?, intensity?, mode?, fidelity? }` | `{ text, provider, model, mode, cardId, fidelity, intensity, elapsedMs, facts }` |
| `/persona-forge/cards/save` | `{ card }` | `{ id, path }` |
| `/persona-forge/cards/delete` | `{ id }` | `{ removed }` |
| `/persona-forge/cards/reset` | `{ id }` | `{ id }` — replaces the user card with the bundled one |
| `/persona-forge/cards/diff` | `{}` | `{ rows: [{ id, name, bundledName, changed }] }` — only cards that differ |
| `/persona-forge/cards/draft` | `{ brief, sessionId? }` | `{ card, provider, model, elapsedMs }` — a draft only; nothing is written to disk |
| `/persona-forge/reveal` | `{}` | `{ directory, opened }` |

Failures use `{ ok: false, error: { code, message?, params? } }` with codes
`rejected`, `no-card`, `unconfigured`, `timeout`, `upstream`, `internal`,
`forbidden`, `method`, `not-found`.

---

The host half declares **no harness package dependency and no third-party
dependency**: it reaches `llm`, `sessions`, `agentDefaultModel` and `webServer`
through `ctx.get` with explicit absence handling, and it parses cards with its
own bundled YAML reader. That keeps it loadable across harness releases whose
package layout differs, keeps it from failing to activate on a composition
missing one of those services, and means a `link:`-ed local checkout works
without a separate install step. Model-route resolution prefers the session's
own last request header and falls back to the harness default model.

The client half imports no harness Client package and is hand-written against
theme tokens (`--dsw-alias-*`) only, so a renamed internal degrades appearance
rather than blanking the slot.

Developed and verified against dsh `0.2.0-rc.2`.

---

```
node scripts/check.mjs        # offline unit check: parser, cards, prompts, client syntax
node scripts/host-check.mjs   # host integration check: mounts the real plugin over a socket
npm run check                 # both
```

`check.mjs` needs no harness and no model. It covers the built-in YAML reader
(including its refusals and dump/parse round trips), card normalization, the
bundled cards' fact preservation, prompt construction, output normalization,
the local fact comparison, route resolution order, the send-gesture decision,
and client-bundle syntax.

`host-check.mjs` mounts the real plugin entry on a stub Cordis context and
drives the real HTTP routes over a real socket, with a stubbed `llm` service.
It covers route registration, session-model resolution, template mode, the
loopback fence, and the save/delete round trip — the things a unit check
cannot reach. It points `DSH_HOME` at a temporary directory, so it never
touches your real cards.

The plugin ships its own YAML reader (`lib/yaml.js`) rather than depending on a
YAML library. A published plugin declares its dependencies, but a locally
`link:`-ed plugin does not get them installed, so a library import would work
only when some unrelated package happened to hoist one.

The reader supports the subset cards need — block mappings and sequences,
block scalars (`|`, `|-`, `|+`, `>`, …), quoted and plain scalars, booleans,
null and comments — and **refuses** what it cannot read faithfully: flow
collections, anchors, aliases, tags, merge keys and multi-document streams.
Refusing is deliberate. Silently misreading a card would give you a persona
that does not match the file you wrote, which is worse than an error message
naming the line.

| Path | Role |
|---|---|
| `lib/index.js` | Host entry: card store, directory watcher, route registration |
| `lib/store.js` | Card loading, normalization, save/delete |
| `lib/yaml.js` | The built-in YAML subset reader and writer |
| `lib/prompts.js` | Rewrite system prompt, draft framing, AI-draft prompt |
| `lib/rewrite.js` | The model calls and output normalization |
| `lib/routes.js` | HTTP routes and session-model resolution |
| `lib/loopback.js` | The loopback trust fence |
| `lib/client.js` | Browser half: composer control, review panel, settings page |
| `cards/` | Bundled character cards (read-only; a user card of the same id shadows one) |
